title: Exchange on a geometric stalk
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme, $X=\mathbf P^1_S=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};S)$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] with projection $p:X\to S$, let $g:T\to S$ be a morphism of schemes, and let $\square$ be the cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with $X'=\mathbf P^1_T$, $p':X'\to T$ its projection and $g':X'\to X$ the induced map. Let $F$ be a torsion abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf] on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], let $q\ge0$, and let
$$\Ex^q:g^{-1}R^qp_*F\longrightarrow R^qp'_*g'^{-1}F$$
be the degree-$q$ exchange map, i.e. $\mathcal H^q$ of the derived exchange morphism $\Ex_{\square,F}$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] composed with the identification $\mathcal H^q(g^{-1}Rp_*F)=g^{-1}R^qp_*F$ ($g^{-1}$ is exact; $R^qp_*$ as in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]).

Let $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point] lying over $t$, and $\bar s=g\circ\bar t$, lying over $s=g(t)$. As in [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality], let $A=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{S,\bar s}$ and $B=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{T,\bar t}$ be the strict henselizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], with residue fields $\kappa(\bar s)\subset\kappa(\bar t)\subset\Omega$ (the separable algebraic closures of $\kappa(s)$ and $\kappa(t)$ in $\Omega$), and $h:A\to B$ the local homomorphism over $g$ inducing this inclusion. Write $\pi_A:\mathbf P^1_A\to X$ and $\pi_B:\mathbf P^1_B\to X'$ for the base changes of $\operatorname{Spec}A\to S$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B\to T$, $\tilde h:\mathbf P^1_B\to\mathbf P^1_A$ for the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}h$, $i_A:\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(\bar s)}\to\mathbf P^1_A$ and $i_B:\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(\bar t)}\to\mathbf P^1_B$ for the closed fibres, and $h_0:\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(\bar t)}\to\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(\bar s)}$ for the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\bar t)\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\bar s)$; then $g'\pi_B=\pi_A\tilde h$ and $\tilde hi_B=i_Ah_0$. Put $F_A=\pi_A^{-1}F$, $F_0=i_A^{-1}F_A$, $F'_B=\pi_B^{-1}g'^{-1}F\cong\tilde h^{-1}F_A$ and $F'_0=i_B^{-1}F'_B\cong h_0^{-1}F_0$ (inverse images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], identified by the canonical isomorphisms of composite inverse images). Then:

1. The maps
$$c_S:(g^{-1}R^qp_*F)_{\bar t}\xrightarrow{\ \sigma\ }(R^qp_*F)_{\bar s}\xrightarrow{\ \Phi_S\ }H^q(\mathbf P^1_A,F_A)\xrightarrow{\ i_A^*\ }H^q(\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(\bar s)},F_0),$$
$$c_T:(R^qp'_*g'^{-1}F)_{\bar t}\xrightarrow{\ \Phi_T\ }H^q(\mathbf P^1_B,F'_B)\xrightarrow{\ i_B^*\ }H^q(\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(\bar t)},F'_0)$$
are isomorphisms, where stalks are those of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], $\sigma$ is the stalk-of-inverse-image identification, $\Phi_S,\Phi_T$ are the strict-henselization stalk maps (the colimit, over affine pointed etale neighbourhoods $(V,\bar v)$, of the pullback maps $H^q(X\times_SV,F)\to H^q(\mathbf P^1_A,F_A)$, and likewise over $T$), and $i_A^*,i_B^*$ are the pullbacks to the closed fibres [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] (cohomology as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]).
2. The stalk of the exchange map is induced by the base change of $\mathbf P^1$ along $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$: $\Phi_T\circ(\Ex^q)_{\bar t}=\tilde h^*\circ\Phi_S\circ\sigma$.
3. Hence $c_T\circ(\Ex^q)_{\bar t}=h_0^*\circ c_S$: up to the isomorphisms $c_S$, $c_T$, the stalk $(\Ex^q)_{\bar t}$ is the restriction (pullback) map
$$h_0^*:H^q(\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(\bar s)},F_0)\longrightarrow H^q(\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(\bar t)},h_0^{-1}F_0)=H^q(\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(\bar t)},F'_0)$$
along $\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(\bar t)}\to\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(\bar s)}$, between the cohomologies of the projective lines over the two separably closed fields $\kappa(\bar s)\subset\kappa(\bar t)$. In particular $(\Ex^q)_{\bar t}$ is an isomorphism if and only if $h_0^*$ is.

proof.text: *The objects and the field extension.* By [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](1) $A$ and $B$ are strictly henselian local rings whose residue fields are identified with $\kappa(\bar s)$ and $\kappa(\bar t)$, the separable algebraic closures of $\kappa(s)$, $\kappa(t)$ in $\Omega$; both are separably closed. The inclusion $\kappa(\bar s)\subset\kappa(\bar t)$ is well defined and involves no choice (part (2) there): $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(t)\to\Omega$ is the embedding of $\kappa(s)$ given by $\bar s=g\circ\bar t$, and an element of $\Omega$ that is a root of a separable polynomial over $\kappa(s)$ is a root of the same separable polynomial over $\kappa(t)$. By part (3) there is a unique local $h:A\to B$ with $j_S\circ\operatorname{Spec}h=g\circ j_T$ inducing this inclusion; so $h_0$, $\tilde h$ are determined by $g$ and $\bar t$. By [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-pullback] (applied to $\operatorname{Spec}A\to S$, $\operatorname{Spec}B\to T$, $\operatorname{Spec}h$, and to the closed points) $X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}A=\mathbf P^1_A$, $X'\times_T\operatorname{Spec}B=\mathbf P^1_B=\mathbf P^1_A\times_A B$, and the closed fibres are $\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(\bar s)}$, $\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(\bar t)}$, so $\pi_A,\pi_B,\tilde h,i_A,i_B,h_0$ are defined. Since all these schemes are $\mathbf P(\{0,1\};-)=-\times\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] and the maps are base changes of maps of the bases, the identities $g'\pi_B=\pi_A\tilde h$ and $\tilde hi_B=i_Ah_0$ follow from $g\circ j_T=j_S\circ\operatorname{Spec}h$ and from $h$ being local with residue map $\kappa(\bar s)\subset\kappa(\bar t)$.

proof.text: *The source stalk.* By [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar] (for $g$, $\bar t$ and the sheaf $R^qp_*F$) there is a natural isomorphism $\sigma:(g^{-1}R^qp_*F)_{\bar t}\cong(R^qp_*F)_{\bar s}$; on representatives it sends the class of a section of $R^qp_*F$ over a pointed etale neighbourhood $(V,\bar v)$ of $\bar s$ to its class at $\bar s$, the neighbourhood $(V\times_ST,(\bar v,\bar t))$ of $\bar t$ being the one used for $g^{-1}$. The morphism $p$ is proper [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and $F$ is torsion, so the strict-henselization stalk formula [prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] gives an isomorphism $\Phi_S:(R^qp_*F)_{\bar s}\cong H^q(X\times_SS_{(\bar s)},F|)=H^q(\mathbf P^1_A,F_A)$. Explicitly, by [lem-weil-pbc-higher-direct-image-sheafified-presheaf] $R^qp_*F$ is the sheafification of $V\mapsto H^q(X\times_SV,F)$, whose stalk at $\bar s$ is that of the presheaf, so an element of $(R^qp_*F)_{\bar s}$ is represented by an affine pointed etale neighbourhood $(V,\bar v)$ and a class $\xi\in H^q(X_V,F)$, $X_V=X\times_SV$; $\Phi_S$ sends it to the pullback [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] of $\xi$ along $\mathbf P^1_A=X\times_SS_{(\bar s)}\to X_V$ (the base change of the canonical $S_{(\bar s)}\to V$), the map whose colimit is shown to be bijective in the proof of the stalk formula (Stacks 03Q9). Finally, $A$ is strictly henselian (Step 1), so $\mathbf P^1_A$ with closed fibre $\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(\bar s)}$ is the setup of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselian-setup], and $F_A$ is torsion (its geometric stalks are geometric stalks of $F$ by [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar]); by [prop-weil-pbc-p1-strict-henselian-comparison] the restriction $i_A^*:H^q(\mathbf P^1_A,F_A)\to H^q(\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(\bar s)},F_0)$ is an isomorphism. Hence $c_S=i_A^*\Phi_S\sigma$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: *The target stalk.* The same argument for $p':X'=\mathbf P^1_T\to T$ (proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]), the geometric point $\bar t$ and the sheaf $g'^{-1}F$, which is torsion by [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar], gives the isomorphism $\Phi_T:(R^qp'_*g'^{-1}F)_{\bar t}\cong H^q(X'\times_TT_{(\bar t)},g'^{-1}F|)=H^q(\mathbf P^1_B,F'_B)$ of [prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula], described as the colimit over affine pointed etale neighbourhoods $(W,\bar w)$ of $\bar t$ of the pullbacks along $\mathbf P^1_B\to X'_W=X'\times_TW$ [lem-weil-pbc-higher-direct-image-sheafified-presheaf], [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]; and, $B$ being strictly henselian, $i_B^*:H^q(\mathbf P^1_B,F'_B)\to H^q(\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(\bar t)},F'_0)$ is an isomorphism by [prop-weil-pbc-p1-strict-henselian-comparison] in the setup [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselian-setup]. Hence $c_T=i_B^*\Phi_T$ is an isomorphism. This proves (1).

source.place: proof of Theorem Tag 095T, third paragraph applied to $T$ ('By our discussion above')

proof.text: *The exchange map on stalks is the base change along $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ (claim (2)).* Choose a resolution $F\to I^\bullet$ by injective abelian sheaves on $X_{\Et}$ and a K-injective resolution $g'^{-1}I^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ on $X'_{\Et}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-termwise] the derived exchange $\Ex_{\square,F}$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] is represented by the morphism of complexes $g^{-1}p_*I^\bullet\xrightarrow{\Ex^0_{\square,I^\bullet}}p'_*g'^{-1}I^\bullet\to p'_*J^\bullet$, with $\Ex^0$ the underived exchange [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange]. Stalks at a geometric point are exact [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] and so is $g^{-1}$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact], so they commute with $\mathcal H^q$ [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]; therefore $(\Ex^q)_{\bar t}\circ\sigma^{-1}$ is $\mathcal H^q$ of the map of complexes $(p_*I^\bullet)_{\bar s}\to(p'_*J^\bullet)_{\bar t}$ obtained from the stalk of $\Ex^0$. Take an element of $(p_*I^r)_{\bar s}$, represented by an affine pointed etale neighbourhood $(V,\bar v)$ of $\bar s$ and a section $a\in I^r(X_V)$. Choose an affine open $W$ of $V\times_ST$ containing the image of $\bar w=(\bar v,\bar t)$, with projection $w:W\to V$; $(W,\bar w)$ is an affine pointed etale neighbourhood of $\bar t$. By the explicit description in [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange], $\Ex^0$ sends the class of $a$ to the class at $\bar t$ of $(W,\bar w)$ and of the pullback $w'^{*}a\in(g'^{-1}I^r)(X'_W)$ of $a$ along $w':X'_W=X\times_SW\to X_V$, the base change of $w$; it then goes to its image in $J^r(X'_W)$. Now compare the two routes into $H^q(\mathbf P^1_B,F'_B)$ at the level of cochains (Steps 2 and 3 describe $\Phi_S,\Phi_T$ on such representatives). Route $\Phi_T\circ(\Ex^q)_{\bar t}\circ\sigma^{-1}$: pull $a$ back along $X'_W\to X_V$ and then along $\mathbf P^1_B\to X'_W$. Route $\tilde h^*\circ\Phi_S$: pull $a$ back along $\mathbf P^1_A\to X_V$ and then along $\tilde h:\mathbf P^1_B\to\mathbf P^1_A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](4) the composites $T_{(\bar t)}\to W\to V$ and $T_{(\bar t)}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Spec}h}S_{(\bar s)}\to V$ are equal; their base changes along $X\to S$ are the two composites $\mathbf P^1_B\to X_V$, which are therefore equal. By [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] (composition (4), computation through any comparison complex (2), naturality (3), and (5) for the etale restrictions inside $X_{\Et}$ and $X'_{\Et}$), both routes are the pullback of the class of $a$ along this one morphism $\mathbf P^1_B\to X_V$, compared with the resolution of $F'_B$ through the canonical isomorphisms of composite inverse images. The maps are maps of complexes compatible with the transition maps of the colimits, so they agree on $\mathcal H^q$: $\Phi_T\circ(\Ex^q)_{\bar t}=\tilde h^*\circ\Phi_S\circ\sigma$.

proof.text: *The closed fibres.* Since $\tilde h\circ i_B=i_A\circ h_0$ (Step 1), [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial](4) gives $i_B^*\circ\tilde h^*=h_0^*\circ i_A^*$ as maps $H^q(\mathbf P^1_A,F_A)\to H^q(\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(\bar t)},F'_0)$, where $F'_0=i_B^{-1}\tilde h^{-1}F_A\cong h_0^{-1}i_A^{-1}F_A=h_0^{-1}F_0$ through the canonical isomorphisms of composite inverse images, and $h_0^*$ is the pullback of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback].

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By Steps 4 and 5, $c_T\circ(\Ex^q)_{\bar t}=i_B^*\Phi_T(\Ex^q)_{\bar t}=i_B^*\tilde h^*\Phi_S\sigma=h_0^*i_A^*\Phi_S\sigma=h_0^*\circ c_S$, which is (3). As $c_S$ and $c_T$ are isomorphisms (Steps 2, 3), $(\Ex^q)_{\bar t}=c_T^{-1}h_0^*c_S$ is an isomorphism if and only if $h_0^*$ is.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
For $p:\mathbf P^1_S\to S$, a base change $g:T\to S$, and
$\bar t\to T$ with image $\bar s\to S$, the stalk of
$\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,F}$ is the restriction map

$$
H^q(\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(\bar s)},F|)
\longrightarrow H^q(\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(\bar t)},F|).
$$
blueprint_sketch.proof:
Let $\bar t\to T$ be represented by an algebraically closed field $\Omega$,
and let $\bar s\to S$ be its composite. Put
$S^{\mathrm{sh}}=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{S,\bar s}$ and
$T^{\mathrm{sh}}=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{T,\bar t}$.
The map $T\to S$ induces a local map $T^{\mathrm{sh}}\to S^{\mathrm{sh}}$
and a separably closed residue-field extension
$\kappa(\bar s)\hookrightarrow\kappa(\bar t)$. For an injective
resolution $F\to I^\bullet$, the strict-henselization construction gives
the following diagram in $D^+(\mathbf{Ab})$:

$$
\begin{CD}
(g^{-1}Rp_*F)_{\bar t}
@>{(\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,F})_{\bar t}}>>
(Rp'_*g'^{-1}F)_{\bar t}\\
@V{\Phi_S}V{\sim}V @VV{\Phi_T}V{\sim}V\\
R\Gamma(\mathbf P^1_{S^{\mathrm{sh}}},I|)
@>{\lambda}>>
R\Gamma(\mathbf P^1_{T^{\mathrm{sh}}},I|)\\
@V{\rho_S}V{\sim}V @VV{\rho_T}V{\sim}V\\
R\Gamma(\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(\bar s)},I_{\bar s})
@>{\kappa(\bar s)\subset\kappa(\bar t)}>>
R\Gamma(\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(\bar t)},I_{\bar t}).
\end{CD}
$$

The maps $\Phi_S$ and $\Phi_T$ are the stalk-to-strict-local maps from the
strict-henselization formula. The maps $\rho_S$ and $\rho_T$ are the S4
restriction quasi-isomorphisms, applied after replacing $\mathbf P^1$ by its
base change to the indicated strict local ring. The bottom arrow is induced
by the residue-field map.

To check the upper square, take a representative section of $I^r$ on an
affine pointed etale neighbourhood $V\to S$. The left route first applies
the unit $I^r\to g'_*g'^{-1}I^r$ and then restricts along
$\mathbf P^1_T\times_T(V\times_ST)$. The right route first restricts to
$\mathbf P^1_{S^{\mathrm{sh}}}$ and then along $T^{\mathrm{sh}}\to S^{\mathrm{sh}}$. Both are the same section on
$\mathbf P^1_{T^{\mathrm{sh}}}\times_{T^{\mathrm{sh}}}V$, so the square
commutes degree by degree and hence in the derived category. The lower
square is the identical calculation after passing to the closed geometric
fibres. Therefore the stalk of the named S0 exchange is exactly the field
extension map displayed in the bottom row, not an abstract replacement.

split_report.summary: Made the statement precise: the source and target stalks are identified with $H^q$ of the closed projective lines by the explicit isomorphisms $c_S=i_A^*\Phi_S\sigma$, $c_T=i_B^*\Phi_T$ (stalk of inverse image, strict-henselization stalk formula, strictly henselian comparison), the stalk is the pullback along $\mathbf P^1_B\to\mathbf P^1_A$ ($B,A$ the strict henselizations, claim (2)), and the closed-fibre map $h_0$ is determined by $g$ and $\bar t$ (the inclusion $\kappa(\bar s)\subset\kappa(\bar t)$ inside $\Omega$ needs no choice). Proof follows Stacks 095T (third and fourth paragraphs) with the cochain comparison of the blueprint's first proof written out. prop-weil-pbc-strict-local-exchange is not used (a pointer: it is the special case $S,T$ strictly local; the slopmaster2 blueprint does not use it either) and was dropped from proof_deps; uses added: stalk of inverse image, properness of $\mathbf P^1$, sheafified-presheaf description of $R^qp_*$, exactness of stalks and inverse image, the termwise exchange lemma, the underived exchange. New nodes: lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality (strict henselization, residue field, functoriality, compatibility with neighbourhoods; Stacks 04HX/03PS/04GU), def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback and lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial (pullback on etale cohomology, well defined and functorial; Stacks 01F7-01FB). The Lean (slopmaster2) is the existential weak form; see the report.
